hooks: Each row can now see its group. What if it needs the row just before it, like yesterday's value?
You can compare neighbours. Can the same trick keep only the top row per group, or remove duplicates?
You can pick one row per group. What if you need groups turned into columns instead?
Flat data is easy. How do you walk a hierarchy of unknown depth, like an org chart?
The query is correct. Why does it take ten minutes, and how do you read the plan to find out?
The plan shows a full scan. How do you make the engine skip most of the table?
Fast reads are half the job. How do you update changing data without duplicates, using MERGE?
sql-advanced.upNext: Queries are sharp. Next: shape the tables so those queries stay simple, with fact tables, dimensions and layers.

hooks: Two workloads want opposite designs. Should tables be normalized or dimensional?
Dimensional modeling wins for analytics. What goes in a fact table, and what is its grain?
You know facts and dimensions. Do you lay them out as a flat star or a snowflake of sub-tables?
The schema is set. What happens when a customer moves city and the history must survive?
SCDs keep history in dimensions. What if many sources and constant change need a Data Vault core?
Models differ by team. How do you layer raw to clean to business-ready, bronze to gold?
Layers are the plan. How do you build and test them as code with dbt?
data-modeling.upNext: Next: how data reaches those models. ETL and ELT pipelines, incremental loads and safe reruns.

hooks: In ELT the raw data lands first. In what format should it sit: CSV, Parquet, Delta?
Files are stored. Do you reload everything each night, or only what changed?
Incremental means knowing what changed. How do watermarks and CDC find it?
The job will fail and rerun. How do you make a rerun safe, with no duplicates?
Reruns are safe. What about records that arrive hours after their window closed?
The data has settled. How do you transform and test it inside the warehouse with dbt?
The models run today. What breaks when upstream adds, renames or drops a column?
etl-elt.upNext: Next: when one machine is not enough, how Spark spreads the transform work across a cluster.

hooks: You know who does the work. Why does nothing run until you call an action?
Spark builds a plan first. Which steps are cheap, and which force data across the network?
Shuffles depend on how data is split. How do you control partitions and fight skew?
Partitions decide where rows live. How do you join two big tables without moving everything?
The join is planned. When is it worth keeping a result in memory for reuse?
The job is slow anyway. Where in the Spark UI do you look first?
Batch jobs are understood. What changes when the data never stops arriving?
spark.upNext: Next: who runs these jobs on a schedule, in order, with retries? Orchestration with Airflow.

hooks: A DAG is a graph of tasks. When does it run, and what time slice does each run own?
Backfills rerun old intervals. What must a task look like to survive being run twice?
Safe reruns make retries cheap. How do you set up retries, SLAs and alerts?
Tasks fail and recover. How do they hand data to each other without a shared disk?
Tasks pass small values. What if one must wait for a file or an upstream system?
That is Airflow's model. How do Dagster, Prefect and cloud orchestrators differ?
airflow.upNext: Next: not every pipeline runs on a schedule. Streaming and Kafka handle data that never stops arriving.

hooks: You need data in motion. How does Kafka store it: topics, partitions, offsets, brokers?
Data is split and replicated. What happens when a broker dies mid-write?
The cluster survives a failure. How do producers pick a partition and keep messages in order?
Messages are written safely. Who reads them, and how is work split among readers?
Consumers share partitions. How do they remember where they stopped?
Offsets are the bookmark. When you commit them decides: lost, duplicated, or exactly once?
Delivery is settled. What happens when a producer changes the shape of a message?
The schema is safe. How do you count and join events over time with windows and state?
streaming.upNext: Next: where all this data lives and gets queried, in cloud warehouses and lakehouses.

hooks: Three kinds of platform. What shared idea lets storage and compute scale separately?
Compute and storage are apart. How does Snowflake package that with warehouses and micro-partitions?
Snowflake rents you a warehouse. How does BigQuery charge, by slots or bytes scanned?
Two warehouse designs seen. How do Delta tables add ACID and time travel to plain files?
The platforms work. Why is the bill growing, and how do you bring it down?
Cost is under control. Who may see what, and how do you share data safely?
warehouses.upNext: Next: how do you know the data in the warehouse is right? Data quality, lineage and governance.

hooks: You can name what good data means. How do you turn those rules into automatic tests?
Tests catch known rules. What if a source silently adds or changes a column?
Columns look the same but values may shift. How do you spot a change in distribution?
Checks are scattered. How does observability watch freshness, volume and shape everywhere?
An alert fired. How do you find which upstream table broke and who depends on it?
You can trace the damage. How do producers and consumers agree up front with a data contract?
Contracts cover shape. What rules apply to personal data: masking, GDPR, deletion?
Controls exist. What do you do in the first hour when bad data reaches a dashboard anyway?
data-quality.upNext: Next: the data is trusted. Move on to machine learning, statistics and models that learn from it.
